Generalized Hermite Distribution

Source: R/ghermite.R
GeneralizedHermite.Rd

Density, distribution function, quantile function, and random generation for the (generalized) Hermite distribution of order \(m\), in a mean parameterization.

Usage

dghermite(x, mu, rho, m = 2, log = FALSE)

pghermite(q, mu, rho, m = 2, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)

qghermite(p, mu, rho, m = 2, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)

rghermite(n, mu, rho, m = 2)

Arguments

x

vector of (non-negative integer) quantiles.

mu

vector of means \(\mu \geq 0\).

rho

vector of shares \(0 \leq \rho \leq 1\) of the mean that come from events occurring in batches of size \(m\).

m

order: the (fixed, whole) batch size, \(m \geq 1\). The default m = 2 is the classical Hermite distribution.

log, log.p

logical; if TRUE, probabilities p are given as log(p).

q

vector of quantiles.

lower.tail

logical; if TRUE (default), probabilities are \(P(Y \leq y)\), otherwise \(P(Y > y)\).

p

vector of probabilities.

n

number of observations. If length(n) > 1, the length is taken to be the number required.

Value

dghermite gives the probability mass, pghermite the distribution function, qghermite the quantile function, and rghermite random deviates. The length of the result is determined by n for rghermite, and is the maximum of the lengths of the numerical arguments for the other functions.

Details

A generalized Hermite random variable counts single events and events that occur in batches of \(m\): $$Y = N_1 + m N_m, \quad N_1 \sim \mathrm{Poisson}((1 - \rho)\mu), \quad N_m \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\rho\mu / m),$$ independently, so that $$E[Y] = \mu, \qquad \mathrm{Var}[Y] = \mu(1 + (m - 1)\rho).$$ The variance-to-mean ratio (dispersion index) \(d = 1 + (m - 1)\rho\) lies between 1 and \(m\): the distribution is overdispersed but with bounded dispersion, and it can be multimodal. \(\rho = 0\) (or \(m = 1\)) gives the Poisson distribution; with \(\rho = 1\) all of the mass is on multiples of \(m\), so other counts have probability zero. In the hermite package parameterization (order \(m\), mean, dispersion index) the dispersion index is \(d\).

\(m\) is a fixed model choice, not a continuous parameter. Probabilities are computed by summing the convolution of the two Poisson components on the log scale; both tails are computed directly. Random deviates are generated from the definition.

References

Kemp, C. D. and Kemp, A. W. (1965). Some properties of the "Hermite" distribution. Biometrika, 52(3/4), 381-394.

Puig, P. (2003). Characterizing additively closed discrete models by a property of their maximum likelihood estimators, with an application to generalized Hermite distributions. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 98(463), 687-692.

Morina, D., Higueras, M., Puig, P. and Oliveira, M. (2015). Generalized Hermite distribution modelling with the R package hermite. The R Journal, 7(2), 263-274.

Examples

dghermite(0:6, mu = 2, rho = 0.4)
#> [1] 0.20189652 0.24227582 0.22612410 0.15505653 0.09174178 0.04682707 0.02159765
# rho = 0 is Poisson
all.equal(dghermite(0:10, mu = 2, rho = 0), dpois(0:10, 2))
#> [1] TRUE
# rho = 1: only multiples of m
dghermite(0:6, mu = 2, rho = 1, m = 3)
#> [1] 0.5134171 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.3422781 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.1140927
pghermite(4, mu = 2, rho = 0.4, m = 3)
#> [1] 0.8953356
qghermite(c(0.5, 0.95), mu = 2, rho = 0.4)
#> [1] 2 5
set.seed(4)
y <- rghermite(5000, mu = 3, rho = 0.5, m = 3)
c(mean = mean(y), var = var(y))   # theory: 3 and 3 * (1 + 2 * 0.5) = 6
#>     mean      var 
#> 2.987000 5.854002
